query: TC4 (Ti6Al4V) is an unmodified α + β dual-phase alloy whose low hardness and poor friction and wear properties limit its use under extreme-service and high-contact-stress conditions. Formulate one hypothesis for an intervention that could improve its hardness and wear resistance without sacrificing its existing beneficial properties. State the intervention, proposed mechanism, predicted outcome relative to untreated TC4, applicable operating or test boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Low‐temperature plasma nitriding treatment improves the surface hardness and wear resistance of TC4 (Ti6Al4V) by forming a thin titanium nitride layer, while preserving its beneficial α+β bulk microstructure.
generation.material_initial_state: Unmodified TC4 alloy with an α+β dual-phase microstructure exhibiting low surface hardness and inadequate wear resistance.
generation.intervention: Apply a low‐temperature plasma nitriding treatment in a nitrogen-rich atmosphere, ensuring that processing temperatures remain below the threshold that would alter the bulk microstructure.
generation.conditions: The treatment should be conducted under controlled low-temperature conditions (e.g., below a temperature that would induce phase transformations) for an optimized duration to develop a thin surface nitride layer without affecting the underlying alloy.
generation.structural_mediator: The formation of a thin, well-adherent titanium nitride (and/or sub-nitride) surface layer.
generation.mechanism: Nitrogen diffuses into the surface during plasma nitriding and reacts with titanium to form hard nitride compounds. This modified surface layer increases hardness and wear resistance while the low processing temperature preserves the desirable properties of the unmodified α+β core.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to untreated TC4, the nitrided samples are expected to exhibit a statistically significant increase in surface hardness (on the order of a 20% or greater improvement) and a measurable reduction in wear rate under high-contact stress conditions, with minimal changes to bulk mechanical properties like ductility and tensile strength.
generation.baseline: Untreated TC4, which has low surface hardness and higher wear rates under extreme-service conditions.
generation.boundary: The predicted improvements are applicable under operating conditions that simulate high-contact, high-stress wear testing, and when nitriding parameters keep the treatment temperature low enough to avoid bulk microstructural changes.
generation.uncertainty: The exact magnitude of improvement in hardness and wear resistance may vary depending on the precise nitriding parameters and duration; further optimization may be required.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of TC4 alloy samples. Subject one set to the specified low‐temperature plasma nitriding treatment and keep the other set as untreated controls. Perform surface hardness measurements (e.g., using nanoindentation or Vickers hardness testing), wear tests (such as pin-on-disk tests under high-contact stress conditions), and microstructural analysis (using SEM and XRD) to verify the formation of the nitride layer and preservation of the bulk microstructure.
measurements: Wear rates under controlled testing conditions
Microstructural characterization to confirm nitride layer formation and bulk integrity
Bulk mechanical properties (e.g., tensile strength, ductility)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the plasma nitrided samples do not exhibit at least a 20% increase in surface hardness and a corresponding reduction in wear rate relative to untreated TC4, or if the microstructural analysis reveals detrimental alterations in the alloy's bulk α+β structure (e.g., phase transformations or compromised ductility), the hypothesis is falsified.
